newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom seen climbing in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom seen climbing in early trade.

text.p: Shares in the German phone giant Deutsche Telekom AG were quoted at between 32.50 and 33 marks ($21.92) in the grey market on Monday, a healthy premium to the official offer price of 28.50 marks for the share.
Telekom shares traded at around 33.50 marks in the grey market on Friday, which refers to the market provided by brokers prior to a formal offering and which is not subject to official controls.
Deutsche Telekom announced the 28.50-mark share price during a ceremony to launch the shares on Sunday.

Deutsche Bank, lead manager of the 20 billion mark initial public offering of "T-Shares", placed a full page advertisement in Germany's economic daily Handelsblatt with a picture of an exploding champagne cork branded with a capital "T" and the caption: "From today on it's unstoppable: the T-Share".
The mass daily Bild shouted in bold type above the fold on the title page "Telekom: The Stock Market is Boiling".

Commentators across the board stressed that Telekom's 100-million-mark advertising campaign appeared to have done what no other share issue in Germany has done before -- it has captured the imagination of millions of ordinary Germans.

It seemed that the question most commentators were asking themselves was that after the storm of share orders by around two million private individuals could the momentum be maintained and benefit German industry as a whole?

In contrast to the 19th century Italian renaissance-style stock exchange, Telekom lined the front of the bourse with glowing magenta cubes, meant to symbolise data bits heralding the information age of the 21st century.

The words "Here we are..." radiated into the night from a wide-TV screen in front of the bourse, with a Times Square- style clock ticking off the hours and minutes until the stock market's opening, launching a new era in German industry.

Shares will trade on all eight of Germany's regional stock exchanges with the first price quotes expected by mid-morning and will move to the New York Stock Exchange later in the day when Telekom shares are listed there for the first time.
On Tuesday, Telekom shares will trade on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in what could be Japan's largest ever foreign listing.

With annual sales of 66 billion marks, Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecommunications group and one of Germany's biggest corporations. Its listing is second in size only to the huge offering of Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
Bankers have heralded the offering as a watershed event for Germany's financial markets as the enormous public interest in the issue has attracted some two million private investors.

Private investors, stereotyped as cautious and afraid of high-stakes gambling on the stock market, caught investment fever with Telekom's issue, cracking open piggy banks in a bid to cash in on what has been sold as a sure thing.

With a third of the issue placed abroad, the Telekom offering also marks a huge infusion of foreign capital into Germany, a fact that could indicate heightened interest by foreign investors in German share issues.
While some analysts considered the issue price to be fair, others thought it was still too expensive compared to other international phone companies and urged caution.

The moment of truth will come quickly enough and investors are bracing themselves for a roller-coaster ride this week as Telekom's share joins the German DAX index of 30 blue chips, settling in as one of Europe's most highly-valued public companies. ($ = 1.505 German Marks)
